Assess a capsule in one call

Source: R/report.R
cpsrpt.Rd

Runs the checks this package provides over one data frame and collects the findings into a single report: the structural schema check, the distributional comparison against a reference, the missingness picture, the multivariate outliers, a Benford screen on the wide numeric columns, and the integrity digests. Use it as the first look at a capsule or a fresh extract, before any analysis, and keep the Markdown version (rptmd()) with the outputs.

Usage

cpsrpt(
  data,
  ref = NULL,
  schema = NULL,
  rules = NULL,
  chunks = NULL,
  sig = NULL,
  key = NULL,
  alpha = 0.01,
  maxrowsoutl = 20000L
)

Arguments

data

The data frame to assess.

ref

Optional data frame the capsule was pinned against. Supplying it enables the drift comparison, which is the check a digest cannot make.

schema

Optional schema from infsch(), or a provenance list containing one. Supplying it enables the structural check.

rules

Optional list of rul() objects.

chunks

Optional character vector of capsule chunks (see chnkfile()) to pin with a Merkle root.

sig, key

Optional signature and verifying key, as from cpssign(), checked against the data's own digest.

alpha

Numeric scalar, the significance level passed to cpsdrft(); default 0.01.

maxrowsoutl

Integer scalar: skip the outlier scan above this many rows (default 20000), since it factors a covariance per call.

Value

A list of class c("bricklayer_report", "list"): findings (a data frame of character columns severity, check ("schema", "rule", "drift", "missing", "shape", "outliers", "benford" or "signature"), subject (the column, rule or row count concerned) and detail), verdict (the worst severity: "fatal", "warn", "note", or "clean" when there is no finding), profile (from profcols()), missingness (from misssmry()), drift (the cpsdrft() result, or NULL without a reference), digest (a list with data_digest, and with chunks also merkle_root, merkle_scheme (the mrkroot() hashing scheme, 2) and n_chunks, and, with a signature and key, the logical signature_valid), and nrows / n_cols. print() shows the verdict and the findings; summary() gives the verdict and the count of each severity.

Details

Nothing here is new arithmetic. The value is that the answers arrive together and ordered by severity, because the failure mode this is built against is a person running one check, seeing it pass, and concluding the data is fine.

What severity means

  • fatal – nothing downstream can run as it stands: a schema check or a rule of severity "fatal" failed (for example a required column is missing), or a column of the reference is absent from the data.

  • warn – something moved or is badly incomplete: a schema check, or a rule of severity "warning", failed (a value left its pinned range, a type changed), a column drifted from the reference, a column is entirely missing or more than half missing, or a signature did not verify (or came with no key).

  • note – worth a look but not necessarily wrong: a column not in the reference, a column whose drift could not be tested, a contiguous run of missing values (one outage rather than scattered gaps), a constant column, values beyond the Tukey fences, multivariate outliers or collinear columns, a Benford departure.

How each check runs

The drift comparison is cpsdrft() at level alpha. The missing run is the longest run from missruns() of at least max(2, nrow(data) %/% 20) rows. The outlier scan is mahaoutl() on the numeric columns that are not constant or entirely missing, run only when there are at least two of them, at most maxrowsoutl rows and more complete rows than columns. The Benford screen (benfordtst()) runs on a numeric column with at least 200 non-zero finite values whose largest absolute value is more than 1,000 times its smallest, and reports p below 0.01. The digest is dgstobj() of the data; a signature is checked with cpsvrf() against that digest.

Findings are sorted by severity, then check, then subject. Nothing is written and nothing is fetched. Errors when data is not a data frame or has no columns, and when schema or rules are malformed (from valsch() and valrules()).

A clean report is not proof the data is correct. It means these particular checks found nothing, and every one of them has a stated blind spot – see cpsdrft() on statistical power and benfordtst() on why a departure is a screen rather than a verdict.

See also

cpsdrft(), profcols(), valsch(), rptmd() to write it out.

Examples

set.seed(1)
ref <- data.frame(
  id = 1:200,
  score = stats::runif(200, 0, 10),
  grade = sample(c("a", "b", "c"), 200, TRUE),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

# A fresh extract from the same process: nothing to report.
cur <- ref
cur$score <- stats::runif(200, 0, 10)
cpsrpt(cur, ref = ref, schema = infsch(ref))
#> ╭── Capsule report ─────────────────────────────────────────╮
#> │   Verdict        ✓ these checks found nothing             │
#> │   Rows           200                                      │
#> │   Columns        3                                        │
#> │   Missing cells  0.0%                                     │
#> │   Complete rows  100.0%                                   │
#> │   Digest         f4d14169312fbd9d251a6ab1daffadef         │
#> │   Findings       0                                        │
#> │                                                           │
#> │   No finding is proof of correctness: each check has a    │
#> │   stated blind spot, and a small sample has little power. │
#> ╰───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯

# One rescaled column and a new category: both surface, worst first.
bad <- cur
bad$score <- bad$score * 5
bad$grade[1:80] <- "z"
r <- cpsrpt(bad, ref = ref, schema = infsch(ref))
r
#> ╭── Capsule report ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╮
#> │   Verdict        ✗ WARNINGS: something moved                                │
#> │   Rows           200                                                        │
#> │   Columns        3                                                          │
#> │   Missing cells  0.0%                                                       │
#> │   Complete rows  100.0%                                                     │
#> │   Digest         ecc02c79b75e352ef946af8cde6b1dd2                           │
#> │   Findings       4                                                          │
#> │                                                                             │
#> │   No finding is proof of correctness: each check has a                      │
#> │   stated blind spot, and a small sample has little power.                   │
#> │                                                                             │
#> │   FAIL warn  drift      grade: categorical test, p = < 0.001                │
#> │   FAIL warn  drift      score: numeric test, p = < 0.001                    │
#> │   FAIL warn  schema     range_score: Column 'score' has 161 value(s)        │
#> │                         outside [-0.8488307, 10.90645]                      │
#> │   FAIL warn  schema     unexpected_grade: Column 'grade' has unexpected     │
#> │                         values: z                                           │
#> ╰─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯
r$verdict
#> [1] "warn"
r$findings[, c("severity", "check", "subject")]
#>   severity  check          subject
#> 1     warn  drift            grade
#> 2     warn  drift            score
#> 3     warn schema      range_score
#> 4     warn schema unexpected_grade

# A missing column is fatal, because nothing downstream can run.
cpsrpt(bad[, c("id", "score")], ref = ref, schema = infsch(ref))$verdict
#> [1] "fatal"

# validation rules join the findings, and chunks are pinned with a Merkle
# root
r2 <- cpsrpt(
  bad,
  rules = list(ruleinset("grade", c("a", "b", "c"))),
  chunks = c("part one", "part two")
)
summary(r2)
#> verdict   fatal    warn    note 
#>  "warn"     "0"     "1"     "0" 
r2$digest$merkle_root
#> [1] "271d0c66b493e55e2b9659fda7eddb00b0439d076eb82f36a4b8922d6bd4d062"

# a data frame is required
try(cpsrpt(1:10))
#> Error : cpsrpt: `data` must be a data frame
